knn: PHATE neighbours per point. Lower keeps fine side branches apart; higher merges them into a smoother trunk.
t: PHATE diffusion time. Higher is smoother and more line-like; lower keeps local detail and small branches.
decay: PHATE kernel decay. Lower gives the kernel a heavier tail, so distant points connect more.
n_components: Output dimensions. Keep at 2 or 3 for a plot; it does not change the shape.
n_neighbors: UMAP neighbours. Higher shows more global structure and fewer fragments; lower shows local clusters.
min_dist: UMAP minimum distance. Higher spreads points out; lower packs clusters tighter.
resolution: Leiden resolution. Higher gives more, smaller clusters; lower merges them.
